newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL gives AA rating for Century Enka Ltd.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL gives AA rating for Century Enka Ltd.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Wednesday it has assigned a "AA" rating to the 500 million rupees Non Convertible Debenture Issue of Century Enka Limited indicating higher safety regarding timely payment of interest and principal.

The statement said that Century Enka, jointly promoted by the B.K. Birla Group and Akzo Nobel, a Dutch conglomerate, is engaged in the manufacture and sale of polyester filament yarn (PFY) nylon tyre cord fabric (NTCF), nylon filament yarn (NFY) and engineering plastics. The company is one of the leading domestic manufacturers of speciality yarn.

The PFY industry in India has had a compound growth rate of 16 percent per annum in the past decade. Demand has increased due to a combination of reasons such as a reduction in excise duties, greater demand for cotton exports and rising cotton prices. However, the profitability of domestic POY manufacturers has been substantially affected over the past two to three years on account of an unusual rise in raw material prices and pressure on sales prices. The company is also one of the largest domestic manufacturers of NTCF. Profits from this division have been attractive on account of the growth in demand for tyres for HCV's, LCV's and passenger cars. At present the company is expanding both its speciality yarn and NTCF production capacities, CRISIL said.
It also added that the present issue of NCD's is being made primarily to finance the nylon tyre cord fabrics expansion of about 5,400 tpa.

Net sales increased to 4,393 million rupees during 1995/96 (from 3,619 million rupees during 1993/94) primarily on accout of an increase in NTCF production and selling prices. Reducing margins in the polyester division have been offset by improved profitability from the sale of NTCF to a large extent. However operating profit margins as a whole have witnessed a declining trend and OPBDIT/Op Income was placed at 18.3 percent for 1995/96. Long term borrowings have been consistently declining on account of healthy cash flows and no major capital expenditure. This has lead to a sound capital structure and capitalisation and interest coverage ratios. Total debt/Networth and PBDIT/Interest and finance charges were placed at 0.42 and 4.87 for 1995/96 respectively.
